roadmap.scope: Presentation-tier only: add ONE shared Linear-style left sidebar (crates/foundry-app/templates/app_shell.html + partials/sidebar.html, driven by a NavContext value object in src/nav.rs) to every authenticated foundry-app page, while pre-auth/utility pages stay chrome-free by structural template inheritance (ADR-001). No new crate, no DB migration, no new dependency; the single hand-maintained hashed stylesheet is re-hashed atomically per ADR-004.

phases.name: Walking skeleton — stand up the shared shell on the dashboard (US-01)

steps.name: Walking skeleton: NavContext + app_shell + sidebar + CSS re-hash + dashboard rendered with Home current (irreducibly multi-file)
criteria: RED: un-pend the @walking_skeleton scenario "The dashboard shows the shared sidebar with Home current" (remove @pending). Against current code it fails at the first HTML assertion — GET "/" renders dashboard_root.html extending the bare base.html, so there is no persistent left sidebar, no "Acme" brand, and no Home/Board primary items. Capture the RED.

GREEN (new nav module): create crates/foundry-app/src/nav.rs with the NavContext value object, the NavSection { Home, Board } enum, the NavContext::for_page(&session, active, board_href) constructor, and template helpers (monogram, is_home, is_board); add `mod nav;` to crates/foundry-app/src/lib.rs. board_href is a provisional "/" this step — the real ADR-003 resolution lands in 04-02.

GREEN (shared shell): create crates/foundry-app/templates/app_shell.html ({% extends "base.html" %}, fills {% block content %} with .app-shell > {% include "partials/sidebar.html" %} + a .app-shell__content wrapper exposing {% block app_content %}) per ADR-001; create crates/foundry-app/templates/partials/sidebar.html rendering nav.* — brand (monogram + workspace_name) and the two primary items Home→"/" and Board→nav.board_href, with the .sidebar__item--active class on the current item. Crafter spikes ONE template first to confirm Askama 0.12 resolves the base→shell→page nested-block split; if it does not, fall back to ADR-001 alternative 2 (per-page {% include %}) — a mechanism change only, identical render contract.

GREEN (CSS re-hash, atomic per ADR-004): append the COMPLETE sidebar stylesheet (.app-shell, .app-shell__content offset, .sidebar + brand/monogram/nav/item/item--active/user classes, :focus-visible rings, Linear rail width ~220-260px + active tint) to static/css/foundry.4c43c2a8.css, then `git mv` it to foundry.<newhash>.css and update the two hardcoded literals IN THIS SAME STEP — base.html:5 <link href> and crates/foundry-app/src/lib.rs:284 — leaving projects.rs:958 untouched (verified hash-agnostic). Front-load ALL nav CSS here so no later step needs a re-hash.

GREEN (migrate the dashboard): re-parent crates/foundry-app/templates/dashboard_root.html from base.html to app_shell.html (rename {% block content %} → {% block app_content %}); add `pub nav: NavContext` to DashboardRoot in crates/foundry-app/src/views.rs and have the "/" handler build NavContext::for_page(.., NavSection::Home, ..) once. Keep the dashboard's Quick actions block untouched (additive-only migration).

Irreducibly multi-file — this is the ONE justified multi-file exception: it must stand up the whole shell end-to-end (nav module + two new templates + the re-hashed CSS + one migrated page) before ANY scenario can render a rail. Splitting it leaves app_shell.html referencing a sidebar partial, a nav field, or a CSS file that does not yet exist, and Askama fails to compile.
cargo fmt --all --check and cargo clippy --all-targets --release -D warnings are clean.

steps.name: Rail identity: signed-in display name in the footer, rendered inert
criteria: RED: un-pend "The rail renders the workspace name and signed-in identity" and "A display name containing markup is rendered inert in the rail". The signed-in-identity assertion fails today because the footer has no identity anchor rendering the display name (the workspace name already renders from 01-01). Capture the RED.

GREEN: render the signed-in identity in the sidebar footer anchor via {{ nav.display_name }} in crates/foundry-app/templates/partials/sidebar.html. Askama's default HTML auto-escaping renders a markup display name (e.g. "pwn") inert — escaped text, no live element — so no manual escaping code is written; the auto-escape IS the guarantee under test.
